data.name: Lakshmidhar
data.gender_notes: Lakshmidhar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Lakshmidhar is a compound name derived from two Sanskrit words: Lakshmi (Goddess of wealth, prosperity, and good fortune) and Dhar (abode, dwelling). This name suggests a strong connection to the divine and a place of security and abundance. The name Lakshmidhar carries the meaning “Goddess Lakshmi's abode” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Lakshmidhar usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess lakshmi's abode and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the inner wealth of an individual, which is their virtues, knowledge, and wisdom.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Lakshmidhar" holds great significance in Hindu culture, as it connects the bearer to the goddess Lakshmi, who is revered for her role as the mother of wealth and prosperity. The name is a testament to one's desire for material abundance and spiritual richness.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Lakshmidhar" suggests the inner dwelling or abode of the goddess Lakshmi, signifying a pure, inner spiritual temple of abundance and prosperity. It implies a embodiment of both material and spiritual wealth, and a deep sense of inner peace and contentment. Ultimately, the name "Lakshmidhar" serves as a reminder to seek both material and spiritual prosperity, and to cultivate a deep inner connection with the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth and prosperity, dwells in the heart of Dharma, symbolized by Lord Vishnu as Lakshmidhar. This name signifies the union of material abundance (Lakshmi) with moral righteousness (Dharma).

historical_references.reference: The Mahabharata is an ancient Indian epic that contains over 100,000 verses and is one of the two major Sanskrit epics, the other being the Ramayana. The Mahabharata is named after the Kuru clan, and it relates the history of the Kuru kingdom and the war between two branches of the family, the Pandavas and the Kauravas. Lakshmidhar is mentioned as one of the main leaders of the Kaurava army. He is also known as Duryodhana's charioteer in this epic.

Another reference to Lakshmidhar can be found in the Puranic literature, specifically in the Mahabharata-Vyasa Samhita. In this context, Lakshmidhar is mentioned as the son of the sage Vyasa and the goddess Lakshmi. He is also known as the preceptor of the great king Bhagiratha, who performed a yajna (Vedic ritual) to bring the god Ganges down to the earth. According to the text, Lakshmidhar instructed Bhagiratha in the Vedas and the performance of the yajna.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Lakshmidhar' is of Hindu origin, translated as 'Goddess Lakshmi (wealth, prosperity) bearer'. In modern contexts, it's used in various ways across different platforms. On LinkedIn, it can be found as a professional name for individuals originating from India or with Hindu backgrounds. Lastly, on Medium, it can be found as a pen name for authors writing on topics related to spirituality, wealth creation or entrepreneurship.
